The last part is immediate from the first part and
Lemma <REF_0001>.
Pick a field <MATH_0001> and a morphism <MATH_0002>
which is surjective, flat, and locally of finite type.
Set <MATH_0003> and <MATH_0004>.
The projections <MATH_0005> are locally of finite type.
Since <MATH_0006> is the spectrum of a field, it follows that
<MATH_0007> are flat and locally of finite presentation (by
Morphisms of Spaces, Lemma
<REF_0002>).
We see that <MATH_0008> is an algebraic stack by
Criteria for Representability,
Theorem <REF_0003>.
By
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma <REF_0004>
we obtain a canonical morphism
<MATH_0009>
which is fully faithful. Hence this morphism is representable by
algebraic spaces, see
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma
<REF_0005>
and a monomorphism, see
Lemma <REF_0006>.
By
Criteria for Representability,
Lemma <REF_0007>
the morphism <MATH_0010> is surjective, flat, and locally of finite
presentation. Hence <MATH_0011> is an algebraic stack which satisfies
the equivalent conditions of
Lemma <REF_0008>.
By
Algebraic Stacks, Lemma <REF_0009>
we may replace <MATH_0012> by its essential image in <MATH_0013>.
Hence we have proved all the assertions of the lemma except for the
uniqueness of <MATH_0014>. Suppose that
<MATH_0015> is a second such algebraic stack.
Then the projections
<MATH_0016>
are monomorphisms. The algebraic stack in the middle is nonempty by
Lemma <REF_0010>.
Hence the two projections are isomorphisms by
Lemma <REF_0011>
and we win.
